reader.notes: 05 comes from OpenCore's absent-OPTIONAL arms (input keeps a placeholder store; I-O and extend create the file), and 04 from the one RecordLengthConflicts test on both relative READ paths. Because OPEN validates the record bounds (39), a relative 04 is reachable only through a zero-byte store, and the sequential leg could not be built that way (a reader opened on an empty store did not see later records). The status class tests (CodeGen/Verbs/IoStatusClass.cs), the generated __IoCheck hook (DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery) and the Status setter's permanent-error record are the same code at every edition.

refuter.evidence: runs/r1a-001: 05 on OPEN INPUT of absent OPTIONAL (not created, no USE) and on OPEN I-O (created: r1absent2.dat present in the run directory, WRITE/READ 00). 04 per §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR16 compares the record to the program's record descriptions; because OPEN validates organization and record size (r4a-001: 39 for both), a 04 needs a store with no recorded bounds, as the reader says; no combination with validated equal bounds can yield a nonconforming record, so no 04 is owed elsewhere.
